title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking.
source_locator: bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.09.12.675944v2: Results (DNg100 optogenetics paragraph) and Fig. 2h-j (v1: Fig. 2h-k); Extended Data Fig. 3; Supplementary Video 1
quote: Increasing laser intensity led to an increase in both forward velocity and stepping frequency.
mapping_basis: The paper names the neuron DNg100, which is a MANC type name in type_list.csv.
stimulation: 638 nm LED laser, 1200 Hz, 30% duty cycle, focused at body-coxa joint of front left leg; 5 s stim; 0.03, 0.09 and 0.33 mW/mm2 (strongest reported: 0.33 mW/mm2)
sensory_condition: decapitated, de-winged, tethered on air-supported spherical treadmill
frequency_note: Stepping frequency of left front leg increased with laser intensity (paired t-tests p=0.032 low-medium, 0.352 medium-high, 0.042 low-high); no numeric Hz values found in the text read.
coordination_notes: Methods: walking on the ball generally with a tetrapod coordination pattern; slower than typical wild-type walking. Extended Data Fig. 3 shows stance-leg counts and interleg phases.
n_flies_note: n=7 flies, 8 trials per intensity per fly (Fig. 2 legend)
notes: Text read from bioRxiv preprint (v1 and v2) of the assigned Nature paper; Nature full text paywalled. Split-GAL4 line is not named in the text read (it cites a prior study, ref. 47 in v1/ref. 50 in v2), so driver_lines is []. Locators refer to bioRxiv v2 numbering. effect_on_walking=speeds because forward velocity rose with intensity; walking itself was evoked by stimulation in headless flies. The abstract printed a driver call/rank for DNg100 (see sightings.csv).

title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking.
source_locator: bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.09.12.675944v2: Fig. 5c-e and legend (v1: Fig. 4c-e); Results (DNb08 optogenetics paragraph); Supplementary Video 2
quote: Activating DNb08 produced oscillatory movement of the front and middle legs
mapping_basis: The paper names the neuron DNb08, which is a MANC type name in type_list.csv; line SS70620 is also listed as DNb08 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 638 nm LED laser, 1200 Hz, 30% duty cycle, focused at body-coxa joint of front left leg; 8 stim-on and 4 stim-off trials per fly (intensity for DNb08 not stated in text read)
sensory_condition: decapitated, de-winged, tethered; Results say movements evoked more reliably with spherical treadmill removed; quantified condition not stated
coordination_notes: Rhythmic movements unlike coordinated walking; resembled searching or flailing movements of legs off the ground. Femur-tibia oscillation quantified in front and middle legs (paired t-test stim on vs off: p=0.036 front, p=0.004 middle).
n_flies_note: n=10 flies, 8 stim-on and 4 stim-off trials per fly
notes: Text read from bioRxiv preprint (v1 and v2) of the assigned Nature paper; Nature full text paywalled. headless_surface=other because the text says movements were more reliable when the spherical treadmill was removed, but does not say whether Fig. 5d-e data were recorded on the ball or in air. Hind legs not mentioned. driver_lines.csv lists SS70620 as DNb08 with no other cells; specificity not stated in the paper, so set to unknown. The abstract printed a driver call for DNb08 (see sightings.csv).
